Figure 2:\captionleadTask formulation and coarse-to-fine inference.
Every stage uses a shared candidate scorer.
Choice tasks select a supplied option. Numerical estimation selects a coarse interval and then a fine interval, returning its midpoint. Point prediction uses three3×33\times 3region selections, re-encoding crops between stages and returning the final cell center.

Figure 3:\captionleadArchitecture of MJev-Spatial.
Each candidate is followed by the same End marker. After contextualization by the language backbone, the state at each End position is passed through the same pretrainedWKW_{K}to form a separate candidate key; the final Decide state supplies the query throughWQW_{Q}.
Their similarities determine the selected candidate, with no added prediction head or new parameters.
Native normalization, rotary transformations, and head averaging are retained but omitted from the diagram. Probability bars are schematic.

Figure 5:\captionleadCentered candidate-logit RMS for each head, averaged per QA along the all-head trajectory.
Values share a common scale and measure response amplitude.
H02 is strongest and H11 weakest in all three task groups.

Figure 6:\captionleadProbability-tree example from the first request in the preselected 12-case gallery.
Full expansion uses 91 nodes; root pruning uses 51 and marks unvisited regions in gray.
Both return four points in this case.
Example from Point-Bench(Cheng et al., 2025).
